back: Inputs, tools and techniques, and outputs. A process turns inputs into outputs using tools and techniques.
Business case → project charter → project management plan → deliverables → accepted deliverables → closure.
A document issued by the project initiator or sponsor that formally authorizes the project and gives the project manager authority to apply organizational resources.

front: When should the project manager be assigned?
back: As early as possible: ideally during charter development, always before planning begins.
A documented economic feasibility study that establishes the validity of the project's benefits. Used for go/no-go and to measure success at the end.
Describes how and when the benefits of the project will be delivered and how they will be measured.
The business case and the benefits management plan. Created before the project and referenced after it; the sponsor is generally accountable.
Documents or communications that define the initial intentions of a project: contract, SLA, MOU, letter of agreement, purchase order.
Describes how the project will be executed, monitored and controlled, and closed. The basis for all project decisions; a living document.

front: What does the project management plan contain?
back: The subsidiary management plans (scope, schedule, financial, quality, resource, risk and so on) and the scope, schedule and cost baselines.
The approved version of a work product. Changed only through formal change control; used for comparison with actual results.
Records created throughout the project that are not part of the plan: assumption log, change log, issue log, risk register, stakeholder register, schedule.

front: Risk management plan vs risk register
back: The risk management plan is part of the project management plan. The risk register is a project document.
Raw observations and measurements taken while the work is performed. Arises in executing.
Work performance data analyzed in comparison with the plan, giving it context. Arises in monitoring and controlling.
Work performance information compiled and presented to generate decisions, actions or awareness: status reports, dashboards.
A formal proposal to modify a document, deliverable or baseline.
Corrective action, preventive action, defect repair, update.
Corrective: bring current performance back in line with the plan. Preventive: keep future performance in line.
A list of all changes submitted during the project with their current status: approved, rejected or deferred.
Verified: checked for correctness by the team. Accepted: validated against acceptance criteria and formally approved by the customer.
Judgment from any person or group with specialized education, knowledge, skill, experience or training.
Unanimity: everyone agrees. Majority: more than 50%. Plurality: the largest block decides, even without a majority.
Leading: predicts changes or trends before they happen. Lagging: measures what has already happened.
Specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, time-bound.
Structured: sponsor, PMO, governance board and project manager; typical of predictive projects. Self-governance: the team governs itself; typical of adaptive projects.
Two extra governance components for predictive environments: taking decisions to higher authority, and formal stewardship of project funding at decision points.
